newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks surge on Dow, primary rate hopes.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks surge on Dow, primary rate hopes.

text.p: Mexican stocks ended sharply up on Tuesday in tandem with a rally on Wall Street and expected sharp falls in primary interest rates, with key blue chips leading the charge on favourable earnings forecasts.
"The bourse was livelier today, with the Dow (Jones) setting the pace, as it ususally does," said Gerardo Copca, an analyst at the Finamex brokerage in Mexico City.
The leading IPC share index ended up 56.99 points, or 1.52 percent, at 3,815.53.
The Dow Jones industrial average meanwhile soared 173.38 points, its second largest point gain ever, to 6,833.59.

Money market traders surveyed by Reuters prior to the close of trade predicted Banco de Mexico would assign bellwether 28-day Cetes (Treasury bill) rates at 21.22 percent at Tuesday's primary auction due later in the day. This would represent a fall of 1.39 percentage points since last week's auction.

"Telmex led the way, followed by Cifra. Telmex earnings are due tomorrow, or the day after at the latest, and they are expected to be favourable," Copca said. "Cifra also gained, partly, on earnings expectations," he added.

Telecommunications firm Telmex L shares gained 38 centavos (5 cents) to 16.58 pesos ($2.11), while its ADRs ended up 7/8 at 41-7/8 in New York trading. Retail chain Cifra B shares climbed 42 centavos (5 cents) to 12.10 pesos ($1.57).

Financial stocks GFB and Banacci bucked the overall trend on the bourse to close at session lows. GFB ended off five centavos (less than 1 cent) at 2.67 pesos, while Banacci fell 18 centavos (2 cents) to 16.80 pesos ($2.13).
Corn flour and tortilla firm Maseca gained 30 centavos (4 cents) to 7.74 pesos (98 cents) in brisk trade.
On the broad market, of 108 stocks traded, gainers outnumbered decliners by 62 to 28. Trading volume was restrained at 75.3 million shares.
